passage:
Farmers in a rural area began selling vegetables through an app. Customers in the city could order directly, and farmers earned more than selling through middlemen.
But the system required photos, updates, and delivery planning. Some older farmers needed help using it.
A local school organized student volunteers to teach basic app skills.
The market improved, but it worked best when technology was paired with human support.
Digital trade can shorten the distance between farm and table. Yet an app alone cannot replace trust, training, and logistics. Modern markets still depend on relationships.
